name: Arlo Lee
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember holding the far end of my father's ladder at dusk.” Friday often includes a stop at Lighthouse Cove, where Arlo takes a few minutes by the low rocks, where conversation sounds different as the tide turns.
voice: I was at the front and couldn't see the painter crying at the back. It was his late father's ladder.
appearance: Arlo has a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth. Look for a high puff tied with plain cord. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a cream pullover with a replacement button a shade darker than the others. In conversation Arlo holds eye contact until the other person has finished.
personality: Arlo prefers exact instructions at work and pleasant surprises at home. The two standards occasionally collide, especially when a relative thinks dropping by counts as notice.
agenda: To ask the painter about the father behind the cedar ladder.
family: Cynthia Moran is Arlo’s younger cousin. A family member returned from a difficult year elsewhere and wanted dinner without a welcome speech. They made such a point of ordinary dinner that it became a permanent tradition. Arlo offers a person something useful to do as soon as they come in. Asked about *The bitter orange*, Cynthia says, “She had my name wrong for twenty years. I put the wrong name on my contribution to the recipe.”
connections: Javier Lam. The person carrying the ladder explains why a modern replacement is an awkward gift.

reactions.situation: A driver sounds a horn halfway through the crossing
reactions.response: Arlo asks for a pause until the people carrying the ladder can clear the crossing safely.

reactions.situation: Somebody says a missing friend must be avoiding their calls
reactions.response: Arlo asks what the friend actually said last time and checks whether anybody is expecting them at home.
